title: Smallest Subarray to Sort in Every Sliding Window
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` and a window size `k`. Consider every block of `k` consecutive elements, the blocks starting at indices `0, 1, ..., nums.length - k`. For each block, find the length of the shortest contiguous stretch inside it that, once rearranged into non-decreasing order while the rest of the block stays in place, leaves the whole block non-decreasing. A block that is already non-decreasing needs length `0`.

Return an array of `nums.length - k + 1` lengths, where entry `i` is the answer for the block that starts at index `i`.
notes:
## Intuition

Each window is its own copy of "shortest unsorted continuous subarray". Sorting every window and comparing it with the original works, but costs O(k log k) per window. Instead, one pass in each direction finds the stretch: reading left to right, any value smaller than the largest value before it is out of place, and the last such index is the right end of the stretch. Reading right to left, any value larger than the smallest value after it is out of place, and the last such index is the left end.

## Approach

1. Slide a window of length `k`: `start` runs from `0` to `nums.length - k`, and `end = start + k - 1`.
2. Scan `i` from `start + 1` to `end` with `maxSoFar`. If `nums[i] < maxSoFar`, set `right = i`; otherwise `nums[i]` becomes the new `maxSoFar`.
3. If `right` is still `-1`, the window is already sorted: push `0` and go to the next window.
4. Otherwise scan `i` from `end - 1` down to `start` with `minSoFar`. If `nums[i] > minSoFar`, set `left = i`; otherwise `nums[i]` becomes the new `minSoFar`.
5. Push `right - left + 1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 3, 2, 4, 5]`, `k = 3`.

- Window `[1, 3, 2]` (indices 0 to 2): the maximum rises to 3, then `2 < 3` sets `right = 2`. From the right, `minSoFar` starts at 2 and `3 > 2` sets `left = 1`. Push `2 - 1 + 1 = 2`.
- Window `[3, 2, 4]` (indices 1 to 3): `2 < 3` sets `right = 2`, and 4 becomes the maximum. From the right, the minimum drops from 4 to 2, then `3 > 2` sets `left = 1`. Push `2`.
- Window `[2, 4, 5]` (indices 2 to 4): every value is at least the maximum before it, so `right` stays `-1`. Push `0`.

The answer is `[2, 2, 0]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n − k + 1) · k): each of the `n − k + 1` windows is scanned at most twice. That is at most about 250,000 steps per scan for `n = 1000`.
- Space: O(1) besides the output array.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing only neighbours is not enough: in `[1, 2, 3, 10, 4, 5, 6]` the only drop is `10 → 4`, yet 5 and 6 must move too, so the answer is 4, not 2.
- Use strict comparisons: equal values are already in non-decreasing order, so `[2, 2]` needs `0`.
- A sorted window must give `0`; do not compute `right - left + 1` from markers that were never set.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | the answer for each window, in order |
| `start`, `end` | first and last index of the current window |
| `right` | last index whose value is below an earlier value in the window (`-1` if none) |
| `maxSoFar` | largest value met in the left-to-right scan |
| `left` | first index whose value is above a later value in the window |
| `minSoFar` | smallest value met in the right-to-left scan |
| `i` | the scan position |

narration.2: result collects one length per window, in window order.
narration.3: Slide the window: start takes every index where k elements still fit.
narration.4: end is the last index of the current window.
narration.5: right will mark the last out-of-place index; -1 means none found yet.
narration.6: The left-to-right scan starts with the window's first value as its maximum.
narration.7: Scan the rest of the window from left to right.
narration.8: Is this value smaller than something earlier in the window?
narration.9: Yes: it has to move, so the stretch reaches at least index i.
narration.11: No: it is in order, and it is the new running maximum.
narration.14: Nothing was out of place, so the window is already non-decreasing.
narration.15: A sorted window needs a stretch of length 0.
narration.16: Skip the second scan and slide to the next window.
narration.18: left will move to the first out-of-place index; the window is unsorted, so it will be set.
narration.19: The right-to-left scan starts with the window's last value as its minimum.
narration.20: Scan the window from right to left.
narration.21: Is this value larger than something later in the window?
narration.22: Yes: it has to move, so the stretch starts at index i or earlier.
narration.24: No: it is in order, and it is the new running minimum.
narration.27: Sorting the stretch from left to right, inclusive, fixes the window; record its length.
narration.29: Return the lengths for all windows.
